correctness.rationale: For r>=1, s>=2, the graph has precisely two kinds of maximal geodesic: clique edges and independent–clique–independent 2-paths. The proof counts disjoint occurrences by distinct clique centers, ordered independent pairs modulo endpoint swapping, and clique matchings; every candidate is counted exactly once. Hitting the clique edges forces all but at most one clique vertex, and hitting the remaining 2-paths forces all but at most one independent vertex, yielding every inclusion-minimal transversal. Optimization over the number of 2-paths proves the floor formula, parity alternatives and threshold. A from-definition finite checker independently verified 22 graph profiles plus 5000 arithmetic profiles; these tests supplement the proof.

value.rationale: An established geodesic packing/transversal duality raises the concrete natural question of complete solution distributions on chordal graphs with distinct maximal path lengths. The complete split graph is a canonical non-tree family; the explicit double sum counts every packing and the second polynomial counts all minimal blocking sets. The sharp equality phase s>=2r and parity-sensitive optimal packing multiplicities refine earlier scalar transversal and universal inequality results and demonstrate different behavior within one natural two-parameter graph family.
